reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown note Isaiah, as a faithful historian, simply records the Assyrian officer's crude taunt, not presenting it as God's own pure speech.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Robert Ingersoll pressed the objection directly, branding such passages among the Bible's grossly obscene texts unfit to be read by any decent man.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Robert G. Ingersoll (1879), letter of August 21, 1879, published as "Obscene Literature."

sides.snippet: The words of Yahweh are flawless words, As silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times
sides.verseText: The words of Yahweh are flawless words, As silver refined in a clay furnace, purified seven times.

sides.snippet: to eat their own dung, and to drink their own water with you
sides.verseText: But Rabshakeh said, Has my master sent me to your master, and to you, to speak these words? [has he] not [sent me] to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own water with you?
